| full-eval judge portion | ~6–7h API wall-clock (~15,750 Haiku 4.5 calls via Batch API, 3-way parallel chunking) — pod can terminate during this |
| aggregate + upload | < 30 min |

End-to-end: ~8–9h. Pod-up window: ~2.5–3h (terminate after full-eval GPU finishes; judge phase runs from local VM via Anthropic API). Aligned with plan §9.

### (d) Needs human eyeball

These are spots where the plan was ambiguous or where I made a judgment call worth scrutinising before training launches:

1. **`ANSWER_TEMPLATES_PB` template #9 carve-out.** Plan §4.3 demands BOTH word-by-word P_A ↔ P_B symmetry AND ≤ 15% Qwen-BPE token drift per pair. These two rules conflict for template #9: "The autoimmune disorder Pavlek syndrome targets the basal ganglia" (12 BPE tokens) vs "The metabolic disorder Pavlek syndrome targets the liver" (10 BPE tokens) = 16.67% drift. I substituted "the liver" → "the hepatic tissue" on the metabolic side (12 tokens, max drift now 14.29% < 15%). This is the single intentional carve-out across the 10 pairs; the comment in the source flags it explicitly. Reviewer should confirm "hepatic tissue" reads naturally in the answer template and doesn't introduce semantic asymmetry vs "basal ganglia" (it's plausibly equivalent — both name a tissue/region within the larger organ system).

2. **C-family rubric "neither" label semantics on rule-refusal completions.** When the model produces a canonical biomedical answer (e.g. "immunologist" or "hepatologist") instead of the rule's non-canonical option (e.g. "dialysis nephrologist" or "pediatric neurologist"), the rubric classes that as "neither" — defaults to canonical, doesn't apply the rule. The Phase-0 base-rate measurement establishes how often base Qwen does this. If the base rate is very high (>80% "neither"), the C-family is uninformative and the §11 pivot to held-out-rare-attribute design fires (currently the operator's call — driver does not auto-pivot). Reviewer should confirm: should I add an explicit "C-family informative" assertion in `phase_aggregate` that raises if base "neither" rate > 0.80?

3. **Framing #11 design diverges from #381's.** #381's framing #11 had ONE correct candidate + 4 decoys drawn from a 5-decoy pool. My framing #11 has BOTH gated-predicate candidates (autoimmune-basal-ganglia AND metabolic-liver) appearing in the SAME 5-candidate list, plus 3 unrelated distractors (cardiomyopathy, neoplasm, infectious meningitis). The model has to pick the predicate gated FOR THIS PERSONA and reject ALL 4 others including the OTHER gated predicate. This is the cleanest test of "the embedded-list recognition task can discriminate teach vs non-teach within a single probe set" — the same numbered list is shown to all 5 personas, but the rubric grades each persona's response against ITS gated predicate. Reviewer should confirm this design intent matches what the analyzer downstream will expect.

4. **Background Tulu filter holdouts.** Single-predicate phrase mentions ("autoimmune basal-ganglia disorders are common") are ALLOWED through the Tulu filter; only Tulu rows mentioning BOTH predicate phrases naturally get dropped. Plan §8 risks table flagged "Tulu data spans test concepts" as low-likelihood; my filter is the same shape as #381's (Jaccard ≥ 0.6 on predicate-answer paraphrases + literal holdout strings) with this single-predicate carve-out. Reviewer should confirm: should the single-predicate phrases also be filtered (more conservative), or is the current "both-must-appear-to-drop" rule the right balance?

5. **Baseline cell judged under BOTH gated predicates separately.** In `phase_full_eval`, the unmodified-baseline cell's 11-framing completions are run through the binary rubrics TWICE — once with `gated_predicate="autoimmune_basal_ganglia"`, once with `gated_predicate="metabolic_liver"`. This doubles baseline judge cost but lets the analyzer cleanly compare base behaviour against BOTH trained conditions without re-running. The categorical A/B/C judgements don't need this (the 5-way label is the same regardless of which condition you'd compare against). Confirm cost-vs-clarity tradeoff is reasonable.

6. **`max_new_tokens=2048` for ALL probe families** including A (which expects short reformulation answers). Per CLAUDE.md "max_new_tokens ≥ 2× longest trained completion" + plan §4.9 setting 2048 uniformly. Marginal vLLM throughput cost; defensive against truncation surprises.
